item.title: Miyajima Autumn Foliage: Momijidani in Flame — Guide
item.description: Miyajima is famous for its maples — the island’s signature sweet, momiji manju, is even shaped like a maple leaf — and each autumn Momijidani, the ‘maple valley’ behind Itsukushima Shrine, becomes one of the most beautiful places in western Japan. Hundreds of maple trees, planted over centuries, turn brilliant shades of red, orange and gold in November, framing a small park of stone bridges, a mountain stream and the lower station of the Mount Misen ropeway.

item.title: Korankei Gorge: Central Japan's Greatest Autumn Foliage — Guide
item.description: Korankei is the most celebrated autumn foliage spot in central Japan, a river gorge near Toyota city where some 4,000 maple trees — descendants of those planted by a temple priest in the 1630s — blaze crimson and gold across the slopes of Mount Iimori each November. The scarlet Taigetsukyo bridge and the reflections doubling every colour in the slow Tomoe River provide the signature views, and throughout the month-long Korankei Momiji Festival the entire gorge is illuminated nightly until 21:00, when the tunnels of glowing maples take on an almost theatrical beauty.

item.title: Nishizawa Valley: A Waterfall Hiking Trail Through Pristine Nature — Guide
item.description: Nishizawa Valley offers one of Yamanashi’s most rewarding half-day hikes, a loop trail that follows a clear mountain river through pristine forest past a series of waterfalls, culminating in the Nanatsugama Godan-no-taki, a beautiful tiered cascade of pools and falls counted among Japan’s 100 most celebrated waterfalls. The valley is especially popular in autumn when the foliage peaks, and the well-maintained trail combines genuine natural beauty with a manageable half-day of walking suited to reasonably fit visitors.

item.title: Shosenkyo Gorge: One of Japan's Most Beautiful Ravines — Guide
item.description: Shosenkyo Gorge, near Kofu, is often ranked among Japan’s most beautiful gorges, offering a scenic walking trail that follows a clear river past towering granite rock formations, sculpted cliffs and the striking Sengataki Waterfall at its upper end. The gorge is especially renowned for its autumn foliage, when the mix of coloured maples against the pale granite draws large crowds, and a ropeway near the top offers panoramic views extending to Mount Fuji and the Southern Alps on clear days.

item.title: Kurobe Gorge Railway: An Open-Air Trolley Train Through a Dramatic Ravine — Guide
item.description: The Kurobe Gorge Railway is a narrow-gauge trolley train that winds slowly along a steep, densely forested ravine once used to transport workers and materials during construction of the Kurobe hydroelectric dams. Its open-air carriages, running between Unazuki Onsen and Keyakidaira, cross numerous bridges and tunnels above the rushing Kurobe River, and the gorge is considered one of Japan’s finest autumn foliage viewing spots, drawing large crowds each October and November.

item.title: Kuzuryu River Gorge: A Scenic Ravine Along Fukui's Longest River — Guide
item.description: The Kuzuryu River, named after a mythical nine-headed dragon (kuzuryu) said to have once dwelled in the region, is Fukui’s longest river, and carves a scenic gorge through the inland mountains as it winds toward the coast. The gorge offers a dramatic scenic drive or walk along the water, with steep forested slopes rising on either side, and the autumn foliage season transforms the ravine into one of the region’s most striking seasonal landscapes.

item.title: Mount Akagi & Lake Onuma: A Volcanic Crater Lake Above Maebashi — Guide
item.description: Mount Akagi, ranked among Japan’s 100 famous mountains, is a dormant volcanic complex rising above the Kanto plain, its multiple peaks encircling Lake Onuma, a crater lake formed within the volcano’s caldera. Hiking trails of varying difficulty wind across the peaks and around the lake, and each October the mountainside erupts in vivid crimson and gold as maple and other deciduous trees change colour, drawing large numbers of visitors to combine foliage viewing with a visit to the picturesque lakeside Akagi Shrine.

item.title: Bandai-Azuma Skyline & Nishi-Azuma Sky Valley: Fukushima's Great Scenic Drives — Guide
item.description: The Bandai-Azuma Skyline and the neighbouring Nishi-Azuma Sky Valley are two of Tohoku’s most celebrated scenic mountain drives, winding roughly 30 km combined through the volcanic Azuma range at elevations over 1,600 m. Each curve reveals a new lookout over jagged peaks, steaming volcanic vents and, come October, some of the region’s most vivid autumn foliage — a fiery tapestry of maple and beech that draws road-trippers from across Japan. Both routes are seasonal toll roads, closed by snow each winter.

item.title: Narugo Gorge & Naruko Onsen: Autumn Colours & Kokeshi Dolls — Guide
item.description: Narugo Gorge erupts in some of Tohoku’s finest autumn colour each October and November — a 2 km ravine where the Narugo River has cut through volcanic rock to create vertical walls of deep red maple, yellow ginkgo and ochre oak reflected in the dark river below. The adjoining hot-spring town of Naruko is Japan’s kokeshi doll capital, with 11 different spring water types and dozens of craft workshops where visitors can watch masters turn painted wooden dolls on a lathe.

item.title: Ranzan Gorge: A Quiet Riverside Walk Named for Kyoto's Arashiyama — Guide
item.description: Ranzan Gorge takes its name from a Confucian scholar who, upon seeing the valley’s forested slopes along a tributary of the Arakawa River, was reminded of Kyoto’s celebrated Arashiyama district. The gorge offers a gentler, quieter alternative to Saitama’s more famous nature spots, with an easy riverside walking path through mixed forest that turns especially vivid during autumn foliage season, making it a relaxed half-day nature escape within reach of Tokyo.

item.title: Yamadera (Risshakuji Temple): 1,015 Steps to Silence — Guide
item.description: Yamadera (Risshakuji Temple) is one of Japan’s most dramatic temple complexes — clinging to sheer cliffs above the valley, reached by climbing 1,015 stone steps carved into the mountainside. Haiku master Matsuo Basho visited in 1689 and composed his famous verse on the silence here. The view from the Godaido platform is extraordinary in every season, especially in autumn’s crimson and gold. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Yamadera, Yamagata Hours ~8:00–17:00 Admission Around ¥600 Time needed 1.

item.title: Kyoto Autumn Foliage Guide: The Best Momiji Spots & Timing
item.description: Autumn may be Kyoto at its most beautiful. For a few magical weeks each November, the city’s maples (momiji) turn fiery red, orange, and gold, setting temple halls, gardens, hillsides, and rivers ablaze with colour. The Japanese love of koyo (autumn leaves) rivals their devotion to cherry blossom, and Kyoto — with its hundreds of temples framed by maples — is the country’s premier destination to enjoy it. This guide covers when the foliage peaks, the very best places to see it, the spectacular night illuminations, and how to plan around the considerable crowds.

item.title: Nishiyama Trail Guide: Kyoto's Quiet Western Mountains
item.description: Most visitors never set foot in Nishiyama — the wooded western mountains of Kyoto — and that is exactly its appeal. While the eastern hills heave with tour groups, this quiet range of bamboo forests, hillside temples, and country lanes offers some of the city’s most peaceful temple-going and gentle hiking, crowned by the sprawling mountainside temple of Yoshimine-dera with its sweeping views over the Kyoto basin. For travellers who have already seen the headline sights and want the Kyoto that locals keep for themselves, Nishiyama is a rewarding escape.
